_comment: restore-drill config. Keys starting with an underscore are comments. Relative paths resolve against this file. Run: restore-drill run

defaults._comment: Applied to every drill that supports the option, unless the drill sets its own.

notify._comment: All optional. A webhook gets JSON on failure and on recovery. ping_* are healthchecks.io style GETs. ntfy is a topic URL.

drills._comment: file: newest match must exist, be non-empty, recent, and not much smaller than the last good run.
drills.name: app-dump

drills._comment: sqlite: a private copy is opened read-only; integrity_check must pass, then your checks.
drills.name: app-db

drills._comment: sqlite behind age encryption and gzip. Steps run in this order: decrypt, decompress, check.
drills.name: vault-db

drills._comment: tar: list, extract to a temp dir, then require these paths (globs allowed). .zip works too.
drills.name: site-files

drills._comment: restic: restores the latest snapshot into a temp dir, then restic check --read-data-subset. source is the repository. Paths are as stored in the snapshot, without the leading slash.
drills.name: nas-restic

drills._comment: pg_dump: pg_restore --list must work. restore_url (optional) points at a scratch server; a throwaway database is created there and dropped afterwards.
drills.name: postgres

drills._comment: command: anything else. Runs in a private temp dir ($RESTORE_DRILL_TMP). With a source, $RESTORE_DRILL_FILE is a private copy of the newest backup. Pass on exit 0.
drills.name: custom-check
